root_cause.text: The RDMA/uverbs function `ib_uverbs_post_send()` fails to validate the userspace-supplied `wqe_size` field before passing it to `kmalloc()` and using the allocated buffer as a `struct ib_uverbs_send_wr`, leading to out-of-bounds reads when the size is too small or warning/DoS when excessively large.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (cmd.wqe_size < sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr)) return -EINVAL;` and changes the allocation to include `__GFP_NOWARN` to suppress warnings from large sizes. The CVE description explicitly states that a small `wqe_size` (e.g., 1) causes `kmalloc` to succeed but subsequent reads of `user_wr->opcode`, `user_wr->num_sge`, etc. go beyond the allocated buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds read that could leak kernel memory. This mirrors the existing validation in `ib_uverbs_unmarshall_recv()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add guard to validate wqe_size and suppress allocation failure warnings with __GFP_NOWARN.
intent_record.what: Added a check that cmd.wqe_size must be at least sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr), returning -EINVAL if not, and added __GFP_NOWARN flag to the subsequent kmalloc call.
intent_record.how: Prevents potential use of an undersized buffer in the send work request, avoiding memory corruption or out-of-bounds access. Also suppresses kernel warning messages when the allocation fails.
